page.layout: One page of text, a single column of verse. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Below the previous poem's last stanza, a title line for the next poem, then verse stanzas. A closing line of initials on the right, and a gathering signature at the foot.

p.i: Ut plena tandem diuitijs domus Amplis nitescat: quid facere hunc putas? Infanus, in se tollit ipsum Tecta graui ruitura lapsu.

Sacrata summo carmina Numini, Fauete linguis, dicere gestio. Caliginosa noctis atras Sol velut exoriens tenebras Detergit, idem torridulus leues Rores reforbet, quum caput altius Illustrat urbes, pellit umbras Quum medio nitet orbe cæli. Sic vera virtus, quæ sapientium Accensa puris pectoribus viget, Caliginosa caciores [?] Inscitiæ tenebras repellet: Et rore quouis delitias magis Perdet fugaces: quæque animum leues Umbræ fatigant vanitatis Ætherea face dissipabit.

page.notes: The verse on this page is set in italic. The opening four lines are the end of a poem begun on the previous page. Doubtful readings: "caciores" (line 11 of the third stanza) is not certain and is marked [?]; "cæli" is read from the ligature as æ. "Inscitiæ" is read as "Infcitiæ" in the print, with the long s as "f" (a printing reading of the ligature). The page number has a trailing dot in the print, not transcribed. The ornamental initial before "Accensa" and "Ætherea" is not transcribed as a separate letter.
